headline: Markets brace for Nvidia's verdict as chip selloff meets hawkish Fed
body: Equities head into today's session still shaking off Monday's sharp pullback, when the S&P 500 fell 1.9% to 7,416.59, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.5% to 24,509.76, and the Dow lost 1.4% to 51,608.17 on renewed selling in AI and semiconductor names — the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index alone fell more than 5%. The proximate trigger was reporting that Washington plans additional restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips, reviving the valuation and policy-risk questions that have dogged the sector since early November. The selling spread overseas, with South Korea's Kospi down over 2.5% and Australia's ASX 200 off nearly 1.8%, though India's Sensex bucked the trend with a modest gain. Attention now centers on Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter results, due after today's close — widely framed as the next real test of whether AI-spending conviction can stabilize after a drawdown that has already erased a chunk of the stock's 2026 gains.

Underneath the equity story, the rates backdrop has turned more hawkish than dovish: CME FedWatch pricing has recently shown a strong majority leaning toward a December Fed rate hike rather than a cut, a sharp reversal from the easing bets dominant earlier this cycle, and the dollar has pushed to roughly a 19-month high as yields climb. That combination — tighter policy expectations layered on an AI-led tech selloff — reads as a concentrated risk-off tilt in chips and AI infrastructure rather than a broad, indiscriminate flight from stocks. Retail-sentiment signals specific to today were thin in available sources; the most recent concrete readings, several weeks old, still showed retail options flow skewed toward call-buying in semiconductors, so today's take leans more on price action and macro headlines than on fresh social-sentiment chatter.
